messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - next steps

Thanks for the call this morning, Mike - good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a dedicated capacity validation run.

Recap of FinTechCo needs from our notes:
- Primary SLOs: p95 end-to-end latency \u2264 250ms for standard generation flows (prompt+response ~ 512 tokens).
- Streaming requirement: token-by-token streaming for live assistant; target token-latency p50 \u2264 50ms with sustained concurrency of ~40 simultaneous streams.
- Peak throughput: ~3,500 tokens/sec (bursts up to ~5k tokens/sec) during morning trading window. Baseline sustained: ~1,000 tokens/sec.
- Average response length: ~200-400 tokens; typical prompt length ~128 tokens.
- Model family: finetuned Llama2-13B (causal), FP16/INT8 quant profiles considered.

Ask from our side: please confirm typical batch of prompts per request (single-turn vs multi-turn), and whether streaming is required for all routes or just chat/live assistant routes. If you can share a short sample trace (logs or sizes), that helps sizing.

Proposed validation plan:
1) Run a two-day dedicated capacity validation comparing H100 vs A100 configurations: measure p50/p95 latency, throughput, and concurrency behavior while exercising streaming.
2) Reserved throughput targets to test: 1k, 3.5k, 5k tokens/sec.
3) We'll provide recommended GPU counts and reserved throughput profiles for your SLOs + a MAP for go-to-prod.

Next steps: if that sounds right, I'll loop in our performance engineer (Aditya) and infra lead (Rafael) to propose a detailed runbook and dates. Also attaching a quick sizing workbook (FinTechCo-dedicated-sizing-v1.xlsx) to capture the sample inputs.

Regards,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - that matches our notes. A few quick clarifications so the validation is representative:

- Streaming: required for the live assistant only (~40 concurrent). Other generation routes (batch reports) can be non-streaming and tolerate higher latencies (p95 \u2264 500ms).
- Typical multi-turn: 3 turns average, history token overhead ~150 tokens.
- Model: finetuned Llama2-13B, currently in FP16 during inference; interested in INT8 to save memory if accuracy holds.
- We can share a small redacted traffic sample (timestamps + token counts) - attaching logs_sample_tps.txt in follow-up.

We're targeting a pilot by late Oct and would like a recommendation for: minimum cluster config to meet the streaming SLO at p95 under 250ms, and a competitive estimate for reserved throughput (monthly commit estimate).

Appreciate the team lining up the H100 vs A100 comparison.

Mike

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - sizing recommendation and MAP

Hi Mike / Marissa - thanks for the details and the sample logs. Based on the profile you shared (Llama2-13B causal, avg response ~300 tokens, streaming for live assistant), here are our recommendations and expected results from a dedicated validation run.

Summary recommendations (ballpark):
- H100 (80GB) preferred path: 2 x H100 nodes dedicated (in 1 or 2 availability zones) with reserved throughput set to 4,000 tokens/sec for peak target. Expected measured results for standard generation (512 total tokens, streaming enabled): p50 token-latency ~35ms, p95 end-to-end ~170-200ms. Streaming concurrency (40 concurrent streams) should be within SLO when using continuous batching + KV cache.

- A100 (80GB) alternate path: 3 x A100 nodes dedicated with reserved throughput set to 3,500 tokens/sec. Expected p95 ~ 240-300ms under equivalent load (depending on kernel selection and batching aggressiveness). Good option if H100 pricing/availability is constrained, but headroom will be tighter.

Sizing rationale:
- The H100 gives ~1.5-2x throughput vs A100 for transformer attention kernels and better token-latency for streaming.
- For 13B FP16 with INT8 quantized runner we typically see memory frees that allow larger concurrent KV caches and slightly better batching. We recommend testing INT8 in a smoke run - expected 20-30% token/sec improvement, but validate accuracy on your finetuned checkpoints.

Reserved throughput profiles to include in the runbook: [1,000; 3,500; 5,000] tokens/sec. We'll run synthetic and replayed traffic (from your sample) across these targets, capturing p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and tail behavior under streaming.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Week 1: confirm sample traces and pick validation dates (we recommend a 48-hour run).
2) Week 2: Run dedicated tests on H100 and A100 configs (we'll coordinate instance provisioning).
3) Week 3: Deliver validation report with recommended committed capacity (monthly reserved throughput), expected SLOs, cost delta H100 vs A100, and suggested fallback policies.

Attachments: I've attached a quick sizing workbook (FinTechCo-dedicated-sizing-v1.xlsx) with the assumptions and a short sampled summary of logs (logs_sample_tps.txt) you shared.

Next steps: can we target Oct 19-20 for the run? If FinTechCo agrees, Marissa can circulate a calendar invite and we'll provision test endpoints.

If you want, Rafael can follow up with a short runbook for enabling INT8 and expected quality checks.

Thanks
Aditya Rao
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
